title: RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture and Phase 4 acceptance run
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the final acceptance gate.

Build a RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture in tests/fixtures/revengGraph.ts containing tmux_lib at tmux_lib, jfred/external/tmux_lib, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; two occurrences each of claude_plugin_lib and scenarios; nested submodules beneath ordinary directories; and distinct parent chains. Drive a full run against it in tests/revengEndToEnd.test.ts.

Verify in that fixture that a change originating from any repeated occurrence converges everywhere; all child and ancestor suites pass; approval precedes every commit, merge, and push; all occurrence histories consolidate into one operation per logical repository; gitlinks propagate through the correct explicit parents to the root; and every intended local base ends at the expected merge commit. Also verify no semantic commit, push, integration merge, base mutation, or archival occurs before approval, and that only successfully published tasks are archived.

Phase 4 acceptance: the recursive workflow is the production path, completes the RevEng-shaped run without data loss, and archives only tasks whose integration was successfully published.

title: Grouping accepts legacy files as modifiableFiles via the shared accessor, and never groups on readOnlyFiles
userDescription:
[split-task-child] This task is being created by `/split-task` as one of an already-requested set of 6 children — skip the oversized-task assessment regardless of this task's difficulty. This child's `files` field must be exactly this list, in this order, and no other files: `["scripts/taskGroups.ts", "tests/taskGroups.test.ts"]`.

Child 4 of 6 from parent task 58 ("Split task file ownership into modifiableFiles and readOnlyFiles, and make briefs point at files instead of pasting them"). This child owns STEP 4: when a task only has 'files' but not 'modifiableFiles', accept 'files'.

Required behavior:
1. scripts/taskGroups.ts declaredFiles (line 16) currently reads the raw 'files' key. Route it through the shared accessor pair that child 93 defines and exports from scripts/prepareTasks.ts, so a task declaring only the legacy 'files' key is read exactly as if it had declared 'modifiableFiles'. Import that accessor — never re-implement the fallback here, because grouping and preparation diverging is the specific bug this centralisation prevents.
2. Grouping and worktree-scope decisions key off modifiableFiles ONLY. readOnlyFiles must never widen a group or make two tasks collide, even when it is ["*"].

Do NOT edit scripts/prepareTasks.ts (child 93 owns it), scripts/approvalGate.ts, scripts/mergePipeline.ts, any skills/ file, tests/prepareTasks.test.ts, or tests/prepareTasksIntegration.test.ts — those belong to siblings.

Files: scripts/taskGroups.ts, tests/taskGroups.test.ts

Tests: group a task declaring modifiableFiles alongside a legacy task declaring only files, and assert they group identically to the way the legacy pair grouped before the rename. Assert that two tasks whose readOnlyFiles overlap — including when both are ["*"] — do NOT get merged into one group and do not collide, because grouping keys off modifiableFiles only.

Difficulty: 2
description:
Step 4 of the 6-way split of task 58. Scope is scripts/taskGroups.ts and its test. The accessor itself is defined and exported by child 93 from scripts/prepareTasks.ts; this child is the second consumer of it.

Why the accessor is shared rather than duplicated: scripts/prepareTasks.ts declaredFiles (line 100) and scripts/taskGroups.ts declaredFiles (line 16) are two independent readers of the same fence. If they resolve the legacy key differently — even by one edge case, such as an empty array or a task carrying both keys — grouping and preparation disagree about which files a group owns, and a worktree gets scoped to a different set than the brief describes. Routing both through one exported accessor makes that divergence impossible by construction.

Fallback semantics being consumed here: modifiableFiles when present, otherwise the legacy files key. A legacy task must group exactly as it grouped before the rename — this is a pure compatibility requirement, not a behavior change.

Hard invariant this child enforces: grouping and worktree scope key off the modifiable fence ONLY. readOnlyFiles is deliberately allowed to be wide (['*'] means the whole project), so if grouping ever consulted it, every task with a default read fence would collide with every other task and collapse into a single group. The read fence must be invisible to grouping.

Source files are capped at 250 lines — split rather than grow past the cap.

title: Reorganize scripts/ into skillBodyGenerators/ plus topic subfolders, updating every reference
userDescription: organize the scripts folder: scripts that output skill bodies go in skillBodyGenerators/, everything else organized by topic (task/, git/, workflow/, etc).
description:
**Measured scope.** scripts/ holds 65 .ts files, flat. References that must move with them: 236 relative-import lines across 96 files (scripts/ and tests/ combined), 7 command paths in hooks/hooks.json of the form `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<name>.ts"`, and 17 skill files whose `!` command lines name a script path.

**The generators folder is nearly empty today, and that is the whole scheduling story.** Only two files match the skill-body-generator shape right now: scripts/reviewPlanBrief.ts and scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts. Eight open tasks — 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 78, 79 — each add one more, one per skill (close-tasks, create-task, merge-worktree-tasks, pick-a-task, tackle-tasks, tackle-unblocked-tasks, update-task-files, update-tasks); 77 already landed taskStatsBrief.ts. Blocking on all eight means skillBodyGenerators/ is populated in a single move of ten files instead of moving two now and having eight more land in the old root afterwards. Decided with the user.

**Four runtime path computations that a typecheck will NOT catch.** These build script paths as strings, so moving a file silently breaks them while tsc stays green:
- scripts/prepareTasks.ts:72-74, `join(import.meta.dirname, "mergeTaskWorktrees.ts")`
- scripts/prepareTasks.ts:91-93, `join(import.meta.dirname, "runMergePhase.ts")`
- scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts:5, `fileURLToPath(new URL("./taskStats.ts", import.meta.url))`
- scripts/reviewPlanBrief.ts:7, `fileURLToPath(new URL("./planReviewRuling.ts", import.meta.url))`
Note both brief generators are on that list, and both point at a NON-generator sibling. Moving reviewPlanBrief.ts into skillBodyGenerators/ while planReviewRuling.ts goes to a topic folder breaks line 7 unless the relative prefix is fixed in the same edit. This is the single likeliest way to ship a green build that fails at runtime.

**What survives a move untouched.** The 14 CLI entry guards keyed on `process.argv[1]` are safe: the `import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`` form is self-referential and moves with its file, and the `process.argv[1]?.endsWith("<name>.ts")` form matches a basename, not a directory.

**Scope note the files array cannot express.** This task renames essentially every file under scripts/ and rewrites imports throughout tests/ and skills/, plus hooks/hooks.json. Enumerating ~180 paths in `files` is not useful, so the array below lists only the files needing hand-authored edits rather than a mechanical rename. The planner and implementer should treat scripts/, tests/, skills/ and hooks/ as in scope for this task specifically.

**Conflict warning.** 27 of the 34 currently open tasks declare at least one scripts/ path. Whenever this lands, every other in-flight task rebases over moved files. Sequence it against a quiet backlog, not alongside a wide tackle-tasks run.

**Taxonomy is left to the implementer** beyond the two fixed points the user gave: skillBodyGenerators/ for the brief emitters, topic folders for the rest. One grouping worth considering that the request does not name: the hook entry points (viewTaskHook.ts, relatedTests.ts, reflow-comments-post.ts, session-end-cleanup.ts, stage-and-summarize-stop.ts, turn-modified-flag.ts) are a distinct category because hooks/hooks.json hardcodes their paths and they are never imported.
tests: No-dangling-reference sweep, as a real test rather than a manual check: walk every command string in hooks/hooks.json, every `!` command line in skills/**/SKILL.md, and every relative import specifier in scripts/ and tests/, resolve each to an absolute path, and assert the file exists — so a missed rename fails loudly in CI instead of at hook-fire or skill-invocation time. Extend it to the four runtime path computations specifically: assert resolveMergeScriptPath() and resolveMergePhaseScriptPath() both point at existing files, and that the sibling URLs resolved in the two brief generators exist. The test must be written so it would FAIL against a deliberately broken path, not merely pass vacuously when a glob matches nothing. Alongside it, the full existing suite and the typecheck must stay green.

title: Give the codex reviewer sibling-task and blockedBy scope so chain boundaries read as intent
userDescription: verify.workflow.js should pass sibling-task scope (tasks owning overlapping files, plus the blockedBy graph) into the reviewer prompt, so codex stops flagging deliberate chain boundaries as omissions.
goal: - run-arguments.json carries a blockedBy array for every task that declares one
- the reviewer prompt names each sibling task sharing the group's files, by number and title
- the reviewer prompt states which tasks block, and are blocked by, the task under review
- a plan that leaves work to a named sibling or blocker is approved, not rejected as an omission
description:
The two halves start from different places, verified against a real run-arguments.json in the taskTools-86 worktree.

Sibling scope is already in hand: verify.workflow.js builds TASK_BY_NUMBER by flat-mapping every group's tasks, so each task and its files are reachable; codexPrompt simply never mentions them. Note that buildWorkflowArguments in scripts/prepareTasks.ts sets each task's files to the GROUP's union rather than the task's own declared files, so "tasks owning overlapping files" is exactly "tasks in the same group" — no new grouping logic is needed.

title: Rebuild the plan review loop on the audit-loop pattern and add a subagent code review of the staged diff
userDescription: the @audit-loop/ approach should be used for the codex review -> subagent fix sequence of the tackle-tasks workflow.
goal: - A rejected plan review leaves a numbered finding carrying acceptance criteria and a required fix, not a free-text notes string.
- The fixer agent is given only the selected findings and does no work beyond them.
- A finding is removed only when it is actually resolved; an unresolved finding is never silently dropped.
- After the implement stage, a subagent -- not codex -- reviews the staged diff against numbered findings.
- On rejection the implementation paths are unstaged without discarding their working-tree changes, and only the findings update stays staged.
- On acceptance the resolved findings are removed and the findings update is staged alongside the implementation.
- The reviewer prompts state that optional improvements are not grounds for rejection, and that a green suite does not make a partial fix acceptable.
- The workflow still reaches a terminal state without a human, despite audit-loop's human-in-the-loop commit steps.
- `npm test` passes.
- NOT in scope: changing the rebase-test or merge stages' own review agents, and the serial-mode brief port owned by task 184.
description:
The audit-loop/ directory in this repository documents a review-and-repair pattern that proved itself on the task-86 audit. Read audit-loop/audit-loop-workflow.md, audit-loop/codex-review-prompt.md, audit-loop/sonnet-implementation-prompt.md and audit-loop/codex-audit-schema.md before planning; they are the specification for this task.

WHAT MAKES AUDIT-LOOP DIFFERENT from the loop tackle-tasks runs today:
- Rejections are DURABLE NUMBERED FINDINGS in a JSON file governed by a schema, not a free-text notes blob. Each finding carries .acceptanceCriteria, .provingTest, .suggestedFixApproach (containing actual code, so the fixer does not guess), and .resolvedBoundaryReference / .resolvedBoundaryExample which must be preserved.
- The fixer is told to implement ONLY the selected findings and to do no work beyond them.
- On ACCEPT the reviewer removes exactly those findings and stages the audit update alongside the implementation.
- On REJECT the reviewer UNSTAGES the implementation paths (without discarding the working tree), rewrites the unresolved findings to describe only what remains, and stages only the audit file. A rejected implementation is never committed.
- The reviewer is explicitly told NOT TO NITPICK, not to reject for optional improvements, and not to accept a partial fix merely because the suite is green.

TWO PARTS, both requested by the user.

PART 1 -- restructure the existing PLAN review loop. skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js:390-403 runs runVerify (line 363, VERIFY_SCHEMA at :87) up to MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS (:279), and on rejection passes verify.notes as a prose string to an apply-feedback agent (:400, APPLY_FEEDBACK_SCHEMA at :99). Replace that notes-passing with audit-loop-shaped findings: numbered, schema-governed, carrying acceptance criteria and required-fix code, cleared only when actually resolved. This half keeps its existing reviewer (codex, with the current fallback).

PART 2 -- add a NEW code review after the implement stage. Today the implement stage (:422-473) produces staged changes and nothing reviews them; only fence violations are checked. Add an audit-loop-shaped review of the staged diff, following the accept/reject/unstage protocol above.

REVIEWER CHOICE, settled with the user: the new code review in Part 2 uses ANOTHER SUBAGENT, not codex. Part 1 keeps codex.

The reviewer and fixer prompts are emitted by scripts/tackle-tasks_AgentPromptEmitter.ts via the emitterInstruction helper (workflow line 40, roles 'verify' and 'apply-feedback'); the new role(s) belong there too.

ADAPTATION NOTE: audit-loop as written stops for a human to review and commit each staged handoff. tackle-tasks runs unattended. Keep the accept/reject/unstage discipline and the durable findings, but the workflow must reach a terminal state on its own rather than waiting for a human.

OVERLAP: open task 120 ("Tell the codex plan reviewer which classes of issue are not...") covers similar ground to audit-loop's do-not-nitpick rule. Check it before planning and fold it in or close it out rather than duplicating.
tests: Run the loop with a reviewer that REJECTS round 1 and ACCEPTS round 2. Assert that after round 1 a numbered finding exists with acceptanceCriteria and a required fix; that the fixer is given ONLY that finding; that after round 2 the finding is GONE from the file; and that an unresolved finding is never silently dropped.

title: Store tasks in SQLite with tags so blockers and files are queries, not agents
userDescription: find a way to store tasks so that they're queryable so that an agent isn't needed to investigate open tasks that block and an agent isn't needed to find the files it touches.  probably needs some kind of tagging system per task/file.
goal: - A query script answers "what blocks task N" and "which open tasks touch file X" from the SQLite database, with no agent run
- A script regenerates a human-readable tasks.json from the database on demand, and the regenerated file matches what the database holds
- /create-task shows the derived tags for approval and accepts user-supplied tags instead
- createTask.workflow.js no longer spawns the blocker-hunter or file-hunter agents; it calls the query script
- The existing test suite still passes: npm test reports no failures after the storage swap
- NOT in scope: the .done file watcher handshake — task 187 owns that
description:
Move task storage from .taskTools/tasks.json to a queryable SQLite database at .taskTools/tasks.db. Use node:sqlite or bun:sqlite — already stdlib, so no new dependency. package.json has no "dependencies" key at all today, only @types/node.

Add per-task and per-file tags so 'what blocks task N' and 'which open tasks touch file X' are SQL queries instead of agent research. The query system should behave like the context-mode query system: structured lookups, not prose. Tags are derived automatically from what a task already has, then presented to the user for approval ("do these tags match? [list]"), with an optional "specify tags" path so the user can supply their own.

Keep a human-readable escape hatch: scripts/generateTasksJson.ts regenerates tasks.json from the database on demand, so a person can still read the task list until the SQLite version is fully integrated everywhere.

Then retire the research agents. skills/create-task/createTask.workflow.js currently spawns two parallel agent() calls through runWithFallback — file-hunter (FILE_HUNTER_SCHEMA: files/description/difficulty) and blocker-hunter (BLOCKER_HUNTER_SCHEMA: blockedBy). Both must be replaced with direct calls to the new query script, and skills/create-task/SKILL.md updated to match.

Existing code to rework: all task I/O funnels through scripts/taskFiles.ts (resolveTaskFiles, readTaskFile, seedTaskFilesIfAbsent) and scripts/appendTask.ts (appendTaskToTasksJson, buildTaskEntry), which read and write tasks.json as a flat JSON array of TaskRecord objects with fields taskNumber, title, userDescription, goal, description, files, tests, difficulty, blockedBy, chainGoal, handoffFilePaths. These become the database-backed read/write layer. scripts/checkBlockers.ts and scripts/getUnblockedTaskNumbers.ts do in-memory graph and cycle detection over blockedBy arrays loaded from tasks.json; that logic becomes SQL. scripts/getTaskDetails.ts, scripts/addTaskFiles.ts, scripts/nextTaskNumber.ts and scripts/closeTasks.ts all read or write tasks.json and must follow.
tests: Seed a fixture task set into the database, run the query script for 'which open tasks touch file X' and 'what blocks task N', and assert the answers match hand-checked expected results, with no agent involved.

title: Add a /mermaid skill that diagrams a codebase into a .mmd file
userDescription: make a '/mermaid' skill that searches a codebase and builds a .mmd mermaid diagram.  it should follow the same mermaid diagram rules that I used for the diagrams in taskTools-86 (Yes/No boxes at decision points, output boxes -> what gets outputted, etc)
goal: - A /mermaid skill exists at skills/mermaid/SKILL.md and appears in the skill list.
- Running /mermaid against a codebase writes a .mmd file the user can name and open.

- The written .mmd follows the taskTools-86 rules: every decision node branches to a Yes box and a No box, every emitted artifact has an output box, and a classDef/class block assigns every node a role.
- The skill contains an explicit written checklist of those diagram rules, and the skill follows that checklist when it draws.
- NOT in scope: changing any existing diagram in plans/diagram/, and changing scripts/mmdGraph.ts. The skill only reads mmdGraph.ts as the parser its output must satisfy.
description: Add a new /mermaid skill (skills/mermaid/SKILL.md, following the existing skill format seen in skills/view-task/SKILL.md and skills/create-task/SKILL.md) that searches a target codebase and emits a .mmd mermaid flowchart. It must codify the diagramming grammar already used in plans/diagram/*.mmd: flowchart TB, decision points as diamond nodes `NODE_ID{"question?"}` branching to `_YES`/`_NO` labeled boxes, plain rectangular nodes for actions/steps, `Receipt: { ... }` white boxes for structured data handed between stages, `Output` boxes for externally visible artifacts, dotted arrows for early-exit/failure paths, and a `classDef`/`class` block at the end assigning colors by role (pipeline=green, receipt=white, output=blue, pass=bright green, nopass=dark red, fail=red). Reference examples: plans/diagram/pipeline.mmd (top-level overview linking sub-pipeline files via Receipt boxes) and plans/diagram/pipeline-preamble.mmd, pipeline-planning.mmd, pipeline-rebaseMerge.mmd, pipeline-exitWorkflow.mmd (each a fully drawn sub-pipeline with YES/NO decision chains). No existing skill in skills/ produces diagrams; this is a new skill directory, not an edit to an existing one. The skill must also carry an explicit written checklist of these diagram rules that it follows while it draws.
tests: Run the skill on a small fixture folder, then feed the .mmd it writes into scripts/mmdGraph.ts. The graph must parse, every node must have a class, and every decision node must have exactly a Yes edge and a No edge.

title: Read the diagram folder for tackle-tasks from .taskTools/settings.json
userDescription: The ability to define which set of diagrams to use for tackle-tasks.  this ability makes the skill and pipeline runner generic, allowing the end user to provide their own diagrams.  the default diagram would be the current pipeline.  .taskTools/settings.json is where this diagram setting would live.
goal: - With no .taskTools/settings.json, `/tackle-tasks [N]` runs the current pipeline block for block: the run-log's ran[] matches today's.
- With settings.json holding `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`, generateSteps, the workflow and the hook all read that folder; the run-log names that folder's blocks and none of the default pipeline's.
- A diagramFolder that does not exist or holds no .mmd stops the run at launch with a message naming the path. No fallback.
- Not in scope: a guide for users who author their own diagrams. A later task owns it.
description:
generateSteps.ts (invoked as `node scripts/generateSteps.ts diagrams/tackle-tasks` from package.json's "steps"/"steps:watch" scripts) resolves the diagram folder from process.argv, falling back to the dead default `plans/diagrams` (diagrams actually live at diagrams/tackle-tasks/*.mmd) when no CLI arg is given. It walks that folder into scripts/steps.json plus per-box stub scripts under scripts/tackle-tasks/, using a hardcoded BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER box-name map tied to the current pipeline's diagram set. generateWorkflow.ts and runStepHook.ts consume the already-generated scripts/steps.json and are diagram-folder-agnostic, so they don't need to change. No .taskTools/settings.json file or reader exists anywhere in the codebase yet (grepped scripts/, skills/, tests/) — this would be a new config file and a new settings-read helper, most naturally added in generateSteps.ts's CLI entrypoint (diagramFolder resolution) ahead of its current argv/hardcoded-default fallback, with the current diagrams/tackle-tasks folder becoming the default when no setting is present.

Setting shape settled with the user: `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`. The folder holds the .mmd files plus each block's script and template. An absent file or key means diagrams/tackle-tasks.
tests: A test writes .taskTools/settings.json naming a temp folder with one .mmd of two blocks and their scripts; runs /tackle-tasks; asserts the hook walked those two blocks and none of the default pipeline.
